To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
haplotypes in 13 lipid genes explain most of genetic variance in LDL (67%), HDL (58%), and LDL/HDL (58%) in 250 families including a total of 1054 individuals.
the genetic variance of LDL, HDL, and LDL/HDL is explained by a small number of common haplotypes in the genes APOE, CETP, LIPC, LPL, ABCA1, LDLR, and APOB.
haplotypes and SNPS in 13 lipid-related genes explain most of genetic variance in HDL, LDL and LDL/HDL.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the major genetic determinants for lipid phenotypes.
the genetic architecture of the lipid phenotypes LDL, HDL, and LDL/HDL and the genetic basis of the complex trait of coronary artery disease (CAD).
the identification of the genetic determinants of lipid levels and their ratio.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the association of SNPs and haplotypes in 13 lipid relevant genes explains the majority of the genetic variance on HDL, LDL and LDL/HDL.
the genetic variance of LDL, HDL, and LDL/HDL is largely explained by haplotypes of 13 genes.
a major fraction of genetic variance on LDL, HDL, and their ratio can be explained by the association of haplotypic variants in 13 genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a large part of the genetic variance on lipid traits can be explained by a small number of haplotypes within the 13 genes tested.
the association of haplotypic information from multiple genes explains most of the genetic variation on LDL, HDL, and their ratio in these representative German family data.
the genetic variance of LDL and HDL can be explained by a few SNPs and derived haplotypic variants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic architecture of the lipid traits LDL, HDL, and LDL/HDL is complex, but can be explained by multiple loci.
the genetic variance of complex traits can be explained by haplotypes in multiple loci, and this approach can be extended to other complex phenotypes.
a large number of SNPs and derived haplotypic variation in multiple genes explains a large fraction of the genetic variance for complex traits.
